sources.title: Aster plan
sources.text: Project Aster retains records for thirty days.

sources.title: Birch plan
sources.text: Project Birch encrypts snapshots with device keys.

sources.title: Cobalt plan
sources.text: Project Cobalt has a quarterly budget of twelve thousand dollars.

sources.title: Dahlia plan
sources.text: Project Dahlia has owner Mira.

sources.title: Elm plan
sources.text: Project Elm has a deadline of November seventh.

sources.title: Fjord plan
sources.text: Project Fjord runs in the eastern region.

sources.title: Garnet plan
sources.text: Project Garnet stores snapshots in SQLite.

sources.title: Hazel plan
sources.text: Project Hazel launches the pilot in December.

sources.title: Indigo plan
sources.text: Project Indigo recovers from the most recent verified snapshot.

sources.title: Juniper plan
sources.text: Project Juniper supports fifty concurrent readers.

sources.title: Kestrel plan
sources.text: Project Kestrel targets a response within two seconds.

sources.title: Larch plan
sources.text: Project Larch exports notes in Markdown.

sources.title: Maple plan
sources.text: Project Maple requires approval from the operations team.

sources.title: Nectar plan
sources.text: Project Nectar grants read access only to the audit team.

sources.title: Orchid plan
sources.text: Project Orchid backs up at midnight UTC.

sources.title: Pebble plan
sources.text: Project Pebble pauses imports while a meeting is active.

sources.title: Quartz plan
sources.text: Project Quartz rolls back by restoring the earlier snapshot.

sources.title: Rowan plan
sources.text: Project Rowan removes expired snapshots after seven days.

sources.title: Spruce plan
sources.text: Project Spruce uses a synthetic fixture for acceptance testing.

sources.title: Tansy plan
sources.text: Project Tansy supports Apple Silicon machines.
